templates.name: Knowledge base
templates.description: Answers the whole organization can rely on: how-to articles, troubleshooting and frequent questions, found by label.

content.text: This knowledge base collects answers that hold beyond a single team. Search it first; when an answer is missing or out of date, add it or fix it.
Everybody may add articles and comment.
Only the administrators of this space move articles to the trash, so a page somebody relies on does not vanish without a word.

children.title: How to write a how-to article

content.text: A good how-to article answers one question a reader would type into search.
Before you start
Name what the reader needs: access, tools or knowledge.
Say which version or setup the steps apply to.
Steps
Write each step as one action, starting with a verb.
Show what the reader should see after a step that changes something.
End with how the reader knows it worked.
Related articles
Link the articles a reader is likely to need next.
Each page below this one starts from a symptom somebody saw and ends with what fixed it. Give it the label troubleshooting.
Symptom
Cause
Fix
What the reader sees, in their own words
Why it happens
What to do about it
Short answers to the questions people ask most. Open a question to read its answer; add a question when you answered it twice.
Read the pages under How-to articles, or search for the task you have in mind.

attrs.title: Who keeps this knowledge base up to date?

content.text: Everybody who uses it. When an answer is wrong, fix it and say why in the version comment.
A few habits keep this knowledge base worth searching.
Search before you write, and improve an article rather than adding a second one.
Title an article by the question it answers.
Label it, so the lists on the home page find it.
Name an owner on the page who keeps it current.
